Platform owns the foundation the company runs on: compute and deployment, reliability and on-call, CI/CD and monorepo health, developer environments, the infrastructure that model training and inference run on, and the security boundaries around all of it.

AI and agent tooling is the clearest example. You will contribute to how models are trained and served here, as well as how agents work inside our codebase: the environments they run in, the verification that makes their output trustworthy, and the review paths that keep it all legible. There is no industry standard and you’ll help form our opinions rather than inheriting one.

Our users are other engineers. Expect to spend time with all the other engineering teams, understanding their needs and building a roadmap. The scope is large, so you'll be choosing what to leave alone as much as build.

Architecture decisions here last: this is a small team covering a large surface. You'll have real room to decide things, and you'll stay close to the systems you decide about.

What you'll own

• Own our platform: GCP, Kubernetes, Temporal, the GPU fleet behind cloud export, and the deploy and rollback machinery everything ships through. You'll be in the on-call rotation, and we'll expect you to make it quieter and more actionable.

• The AI enablement substrate: GPU capacity, training and inference pipelines, and the reliability and cost of the systems serving models in production.

• Cost is an engineering constraint: infrastructure decisions have a number attached and you're expected to make smart trade-offs. As inference grows with usage, the metering and attribution behind those numbers sit with this team.

• Security comes with the systems you run: identity and access, secrets management, least-privilege boundaries, and supply-chain integrity.

• Make what you build legible. Infrastructure-as-code that explains itself. Runbooks and in-repo context written for someone jumping in to help. Observability that tells you what failed and why.

• Improve how the team learns and ships. Form hypotheses, instrument your work, release incrementally, and read results honestly. Strengthen the tooling, standards, tests, observability, and release practices that help the team move quickly without compromising quality.

• Raise the team’s technical ambition. Provide architectural direction, thoughtful reviews, mentoring, and clear human writing.

What you bring

Required:

• You have 8+ years building and operating production distributed systems, or equivalent server-side engineering with a heavy infrastructure focus.

• You effectively leverage agents to multiply your impact and think critically about how and when to harness AI in your work.

• You've run systems where failure was expensive, and your opinions about reliability and deployment come from consequences rather than reading.

• You've carried a pager, commanded an incident, and rolled back before you understood why.

• You use SLOs and error budgets as operating tools.

• You’ve used a major cloud provider and Kubernetes in production, with infrastructure-as-code as your default.

• You've owned an architecture or migration, from planning through launch, whose consequences outlived the project, and you can say what you'd do differently.

• You've found important unowned work, scoped it, earned buy-in, and delivered it without being handed a spec.

• You build a minimal repro, read the logs, and write targeted checks to prove a fix works instead of trusting output.

Experience that helps:

• GPU and ML infrastructure: capacity planning, training or inference pipelines, serving cost and latency. If you haven't run a GPU fleet, experience with expensive capacity-constrained systems transfers well.

• Production security engineering: IAM, secrets, supply chain, least privilege. You don't need to have held a security title, but you should have owned these boundaries for systems you ran.

• Cloud cost modeling: commitment strategy, reservations, unit economics.

• CI/CD: at monorepo scale, and developer-environment work.

• Intricacies of Video: Media, video, or GPU-backed workloads.

• Small teams owning a large surface: whether at a Series B to D company or on an internal platform team.

Key Responsibilities

Requirements & Documentation

Translate user problems, pains, and requirements into well-structured product requirement documents (PRDs) that guide engineering development.

Write clear, structured user stories, acceptance criteria, and product documentation for both internal and external audiences.

Gather input from multiple stakeholders — customers, internal teams, and market signals — into actionable documentation that supports product development and decision-making.

Create and maintain product documentation to keep it current as features and workflows change.

Stakeholder Collaboration

Work closely with Team Managers, Engineering, and client-facing teams to gather, analyze, and document product requirements.

Facilitate requirement discussions and workshops to identify the right questions and bring clarity to ambiguous problem statements.

Act as a coordination layer between product, engineering, and business teams—ensuring everyone shares a common understanding.

Analysis & Market Intelligence

Contribute to market and competitive intelligence efforts by monitoring industry trends, competitor capabilities, and changing customer use cases.

Analyze customer feedback, support data, and usage patterns to spot gaps, friction points, and opportunities.

Assist the Sr. PMs in assessing feature ideas and prioritization decisions through thorough analysis and documentation.

Who We’re Looking For

We hire for four traits above all else. The rest is downstream of these.

Clarity in communication: You can take a complex problem and explain it to engineering, sales, and senior stakeholders in a way that each of them can act on. Your documentation is brief, precise, and clear.

Confident and coachable: You’re comfortable saying “I don’t know” and “I was wrong.” You stand your ground when you have evidence and update your view when the evidence suggests otherwise.

Applied thinking: You analyze user problems thoroughly before jumping to solutions. You work backward from what the user is trying to achieve and notice the secondary questions others overlook.

Fast learner: You quickly acquire new skills, explore unfamiliar areas, respond to feedback, and figure things out. You don’t wait for instructions on what to do next.

Qualification & Requirements

1–3 years of experience in a product, business analysis, consulting, or a related role in a B2B or SaaS environment.

Strong analytical thinking and structured problem-solving skills — you can break down ambiguous problems and clarify them.

Excellent written communication — your documentation is clear, precise, and easy to understand without a meeting to explain it.

Proven ability to synthesize inputs from various sources into coherent, actionable documentation.

Comfort working closely with engineering teams — you don’t need to write code, but you should understand how software systems function.

Attention to detail without losing sight of the bigger picture. A genuine curiosity about how products work and how users actually experience them.

Tools & Technical Skills

Familiar with product and project management tools like Jira, Confluence, Notion, or similar.

Comfortable working with data — able to read reports, interpret usage metrics, and identify key insights.

Experience creating user stories, PRDs, or functional specs is a plus. Exposure to AI or SaaS products is beneficial but not required.

Basic understanding of APIs or data flows is useful; you don’t need to be technical, but you should have a curiosity about technology.

Headquarters: Remote, United States

About Calm

Calm is the leading mental health brand on a mission to make the world happier and healthier. Known for its flagship consumer app—ranked #1 in its category with over 180 million downloads and availability in ten languages across 190 countries—Calm helps people sleep better, stress less, and live more mindfully through content and tools from experts and beloved celebrity voices. Building on this foundation, Calm has created a broader portfolio including evidence-based solutions like Calm Health, offered through employers, health plans and providers, designed to expand access to mental health and sleep support, boost benefits engagement, and drive positive health outcomes. Today, Calm supports more than 3,500 organizations and reaches over 42 million covered lives through Calm Health. Calm has been recognized as a TIME100 Most Influential Company and one of Fast Company’s Brands That Matter. Learn more at calm.com.
What We Do

At Calm we believe in making relaxation, better sleep, and mindfulness accessible to the entire world, and we hope you will help us achieve our mission. The Product & Design team is responsible for delivering Calm to our customers, ensuring that it is easy to use, supports their goals, and maintains a high level of quality across web, iOS, Android platforms.

As a Senior Product Designer on our Consumer team, you'll shape experiences used by tens of millions of people to sleep better, stress less, and live more mindfully. People often reach for Calm in their most vulnerable moments, so the craft of what we make (how it looks, moves, and feels) matters enormously. 

This is a builder's role in the truest sense: you'll use AI and modern prototyping tools to move from insight to interactive prototype to shipped experience, not as a shortcut on quality, but to spend less time producing and more time on the judgment and detail that make an experience great. When anyone can generate a hundred screens in an afternoon, taste and judgment are the differentiators! 

The heart of this role is balancing velocity and craft in service of making our users healthier and happier, and building intuitive, engaging and impactful experiences that drive acquisition, engagement and retention.  You'll partner closely with Product Management, Engineering, Data Science, and Marketing, and set the standard for craft across iOS, Android, and web.  You will be a thought leader in design, helping to establish best practices and setting the bar for exceptional product design at Calm.

What You’ll Do

• Own end-to-end product design initiatives that cover the whole product experience (visual, interaction, motion, brand integration), to create thoughtful, high-quality user-centered mobile experiences.

• Prototype quickly in Figma and with AI and low-code tools like Replit, Lovable, and Claude, so you can get real, testable ideas in front of people early.

• Present your design work clearly and persuasively to cross-functional stakeholders (including senior leadership), give and take feedback well, anchoring your rationale to both user needs and business goals.

• Maintain strong attention to detail and collaboration through engineering implementation (build and QA) and post launch-iterations, to ensure high-quality execution.

• Use data and drive research to inform the experiences you build, and leverage performance insights to evolve your approach.

• Champion system-level thinking (improving how the team works and evolving Calm's design system) so the whole team works faster and smarter.

• Balance multiple projects in a fast-paced environment while maintaining high standards of execution. 

Who You Are

• Experienced Product Designer: 7+ years of experience in UX and UI design with 5+ within consumer mobile and web applications.

• AI-native and tooling-fluent: Highly proficient in Figma for design, and already using AI and low-code tools (Replit, Lovable, Claude) to prototype and move fast, with the judgment to know when the output is good enough and when it isn't.

• Technical agility: Comfortable shipping small code changes without engineering support, bridging the gap between design and engineering by personally shipping copy and UI polish directly.

• A builder: Biased toward shipping and iterating over perfect plans. You'd rather put a working prototype in front of people than write a doc about one.

• Data- and research-informed: You fold both qualitative and quantitative insight into your design decisions, and you measure whether the work landed.

• A strong collaborator: A low-ego, trusted partner to Product, Research, and Engineering who makes the people around them better and helps sharpen how the team works.

• High craft standards: A strong advocate for accessibility, consistency, visual storytelling, brand integration, and motion design to create engaging user experiences, while still maintaining velocity.

• A clear communicator: You present your thinking persuasively to stakeholders and senior leadership, give and take feedback well, and champion an experience while staying open to being wrong.

Nice to Haves

• Experience with conversational or AI-native UX.

• Experience working at multiple organizations, ideally including time at a consumer product in a fast-paced startup environment.

• A strong portfolio demonstrating your ability to design and ship beautiful, functional, and user-friendly experiences.

• Comfort shipping small copy and UI changes directly in code, without engineering support.

• A passion for Calm's mission and a point of view on how digital products can support mental health.

Minimum Requirements

• 7+ years in UX/UI design with 5+ within consumer mobile (and web) applications.

• Proven experience driving user testing and research.

• Strong foundation in interaction design, visual design, and usability best practices.

• Experience designing and shipping mobile applications at scale.

• Hands-on proficiency in Figma and modern AI/prototyping tools.

• Ability to work independently while contributing to a larger design vision and strategy.

Calm uses a geographic pay model that determines salaries based on the location where an employee lives. For this position, the base pay ranges across Calm’s pay tiers is as follows: $168,000 - $245,000. The base pay range represents the low and high end of Calm’s salary range for this position. Not all candidates will be eligible for the upper end of the salary range. Exact salary will ultimately depend on multiple factors, which include the successful candidate's geographic location, skills, experience and other qualifications. Calm uses employee zip code to determine which pay range applies. This role is also eligible for equity + comprehensive benefits + 401k + flexible time off.

Calm may incorporate artificial intelligence technology to support the application review process, but rest assured that human reviewers are involved in all stages of the hiring process.

Calm is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities, including disabled veterans. If you require a reasonable accommodation to complete any part of the application or interview process, please contact Calm’s Recruiting team at recruitingaccommodations@calm.com. All accommodation requests will be handled confidentially and assessed on a case-by-case basis.

Job Description
CerebriOS is a software company building B2B SaaS products that help businesses make better decisions, streamline operations, and get more value from their data. Our products combine practical business workflows with intuitive technology designed for everyday use. We bring together technology, data, and business expertise to create solutions that are scalable, reliable, and easy to use.
We are looking for a Quality Assurance Engineer to help deliver dependable software across web, mobile, and API-based products. This role combines manual testing with test automation, giving you the opportunity to identify risks early, improve testing processes, and work closely with engineers to prevent defects from reaching customers.
WHAT YOU WILL DO

• 
Review requirements and define acceptance and testing criteria.

• 
Create and execute functional, regression, integration, and exploratory tests.

• 
Document defects with clear, reproducible steps and supporting evidence.

• 
Build and maintain automated UI or API tests.

• 
Validate fixes and monitor recurring quality issues.

• 
Participate in release planning and readiness reviews.

• 
Work with developers to improve application testability.

• 
Maintain test documentation, environments, and test data.

• 
Communicate quality risks to technical and nontechnical stakeholders.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

• 
2+ years of experience in software QA or testing.

• 
Experience testing web, mobile, or API-based applications.

• 
Knowledge of test design and defect-management practices.

• 
Familiarity with tools such as Jira, Postman, or browser developer tools.

• 
Strong attention to detail and analytical problem-solving skills.

• 
Clear written communication.

NICE TO HAVE

• 
Experience with Playwright, Cypress, Selenium, or Appium.

• 
Programming experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, or Java.

• 
Familiarity with CI/CD systems, SQL, and performance testing.

• 
Relevant testing certification such as ISTQB.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS
$70,000–$90,000 annually, depending on experience and qualifications.
CerebriOS offers a remote-first work environment, opportunities to work with modern software testing and automation technologies, and a collaborative culture focused on building reliable products and continuously improving engineering practices.
HIRING PROCESS
Application review → recruiter screen → testing scenario or short role-relevant assessment → final stakeholder interview → offer.
EQUAL OPPORTUNITY
CerebriOS is an equal-opportunity employer. We value diversity and consider qualified candidates without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic.

Location: Remote
